title: Clearing Your ITR Backlog with the Updated Return (ITR-U)
description: ITR-U, or Updated Income Tax Return, allows taxpayers to correct errors or report previously missed income for past assessment years. It provides a valuable o.

faq.q: Can I file ITR-U for any assessment year?
faq.a: No, you can only file an ITR-U for assessment years for which the 24-month window from the end of the relevant assessment year has not yet expired. Currently, this generally means AY 2023-24 and AY 2024-25.

faq.q: What if I want to reduce my income or claim a higher refund using ITR-U?
faq.a: ITR-U cannot be used to reduce your income, increase a loss, or claim a higher refund. Its sole purpose is to declare additional income and pay more tax.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to file an ITR-U if I discover an error?
faq.a: While not strictly mandatory in the sense of a direct notice, it is highly advisable to file an ITR-U if you discover unreported income or errors. This helps you avoid potential penalties, interest, and prosecution if the discrepancy is later identified by the Income Tax Department.

faq.q: What documents are required to file ITR-U?
faq.a: You'll need documents pertaining to the additional income you are reporting (e.g., bank statements, capital gains statements, Form 16A/16B/16C, invoices). You will also need your original ITR details (if filed) and the Challan for payment of additional tax and interest.

Yes, NRIs who have taxable income in India and have missed reporting it or made errors in their original filings can also use the ITR-U mechanism, provided they meet all the eligibility criteria and restrictions.

faq.q: What happens if I don't file ITR-U and the department finds an error?
faq.a: If the Income Tax Department discovers unreported income or errors during an assessment, you could face significant penalties, higher interest charges, and potentially prosecution under the Income Tax Act. Filing an ITR-U voluntarily offers a more lenient path to compliance.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of ITR-U, but some key details regarding the filing timeframe and additional tax rates are outdated due to recent budget amendments.
